newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Tamil Tiger rebels fire mortars at Sri Lanka troop.
newsitem.headline: Tamil Tiger rebels fire mortars at Sri Lanka troop.

text.p: Sri Lanka's Tamil Tiger rebels fired mortars at troops consolidating in the newly captured areas in the north of the island, military officials said on Sunday.

The army retaliated by firing mortar and artillery shells at known rebel positions in their northern Wanni heartland, the officials said. There were no casualties among the troops, they said, adding that it was not known whether any rebels had been killed.
The Defence Ministry said troops ambushed and killed two rebels in the Nedunkeni area and recovered ammunition and communications equipment.
Officials said troops were clearing mines and fortifying areas north of Omanthai and Nedunkeni, captured over the last two weeks.

The clandestine Voice of Tiger radio monitored in northern Vavuniya said on Sunday that the military had fired artillery shells at rebel positions and civilian areas in Mankulam, 40 km (25 miles) north of Vavuniya.
It said heavy shelling had forced civilians to leave their homes and take shelter in the jungle.

Two army divisions, consisting of some 20,000 troops, launched "Operation Jaya Sikuru", or "Sure of Victory", from Vavuniya 220 km (135 miles) north of Colombo, on May 13 in a bid to open a supply route to the Jaffna peninsula, 100 km (60 miles) further north.
The Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam have accused the government of killing Tamil civilians and destroying their property under the pretext of opening a supply route.
They said in an overnight statement on Sunday that troops had bombarded Oddusuddan, some 24 km (15 miles) north of Nedunkeni, non-stop for three nights.

"Sri Lanka is using the 'supply route offensive' as a cover to smash as many Tamil towns as possible to rubble. The idea is to create masses of refugees and hole the Tamil people into a corner," the statement said.
Independent verification of the events is not possible as the international media is not allowed into the battle zone.
The LTTE are fighting for an independent homeland for minority Tamils in mainly Sinhalese Sri Lanka's north and east.
The government says more than 50,000 people have been killed since the war began in 1983. The rebels say the toll is higher.
